clue.text: Primary scholar has added, thus

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is the crossword's standard graduate scholar
sic is Latin for thus, printed to show a quotation is exact

explanation.surface: A learned man appends a 'thus' to a text, as scholars do.
explanation.definitionFit: Primary and elementary skills are the fundamental, first-level ones.

clue.text: They are thrown into the water for person in tub

definitions.text: They are thrown into the water for person in tub

parts.words: They are thrown into the water for person in tub
parts.note: suggests lifebelts thrown to someone overboard, but the person is merely bathing and the things tossed in are scented crystals

explanation.definitionFit: Scented crystals dissolved in a bath are tipped into the water for the bather.

clue.text: Phase out riding to get fit

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of the word are rearranged

parts.note: to be up is to be on horseback, riding

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a stage of horse-riding in order to get in shape.
explanation.definitionFit: To improve one's condition or performance is an idiomatic sense of getting fit.

clue.text: Sound of oars heard in this backwater

indicators.note: heard tells us the word is taken as it is spoken, not as it is spelt

parts.note: oars in rowlocks make a creaking noise

explanation.surface: Rowing in a quiet inlet, one hears the oars creaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A creek is a small inlet or side stream, a quiet stretch of water off the main flow.

clue.text: Judge making a bitter outburst after rejection of artist

indicators.note: after places the anagram behind the reversed artist
a rejection turns something back, so the artist's letters are read backwards

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist

indicators.note: an outburst bursts the words apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An artist's rejection provokes a bitter outburst from someone judging.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, Royal Academician, is the standard artist; 'rejection of' turns it, and 'outburst' signals the anagram of A BITTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To arbitrate is to decide a dispute as an impartial referee.

clue.text: Ran down, not initially dressed

indicators.note: not initially says the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: to run someone down is to malign or disparage them

explanation.surface: A runner went down a slope without having dressed first.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers who dress ranks line up straight, so dressed in that drill sense means set in line.

clue.text: Frustrate wicked plot at the outset

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot, and 'at the outset' says it comes first
wicked means evil

explanation.surface: A wicked scheme is foiled right from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wicked plot' reads as one scheme, but the plot is a flower bed, and 'at the outset' moves it to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedevil a plan is to plague and thwart it.

clue.text: Wade with vital contrivance into dangerous water

indicators.note: a contrivance is an artful arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wades with vital equipment into a hazardous sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrivance' rearranges the letters of WADE and VITAL together.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge sea wave, such as one raised by an earthquake, is a perilous body of water.

clue.text: Scared Capone with weapon

parts.note: Al Capone, the Chicago gangster
armed means carrying a weapon

explanation.surface: People are frightened of a gangster carrying a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Frightened and fearful are synonyms of the adjective.

clue.text: Restricted in quarters, archdeacon quits

indicators.note: restricted in means confined within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: E and S, East and South, are two quarters of the compass
Ven, Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon

explanation.surface: An archdeacon, confined to his lodgings, resigns his post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarters' gives two compass points, E and S, around VEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Being quits means being square, with neither side owing the other.

clue.text: A blow for business above or below the line?

definitions.text: A blow for business above or below the line?

parts.words: A blow for business above or below the line?
parts.note: reads like accounting jargon, but a blow is a wind, business is commerce, and the Line is the equator, north and south of which these winds blow

explanation.definitionFit: These steady tropical winds either side of the equator once carried merchant sailing ships.

clue.text: Fly as a bird

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a male duck and an angler's mayfly imitation.

clue.text: Talking books conveying significant information

definitions.meaning: the idiom for something that says a great deal without words

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means revealing much; literally it describes tomes that talk.

clue.text: Make an interpretation of speech, lacking sound information

definitions.text: Make an interpretation of speech, lacking sound information

parts.words: Make an interpretation of speech, lacking sound information
parts.note: sounds like a slapdash reading of a speech without good facts, but describes a deaf person following a speaker's mouth movements

explanation.definitionFit: Deaf people understand speech by watching the movements of a speaker's mouth.

clue.text: Freedom of movement needed by violinist

definitions.text: Freedom of movement needed by violinist

parts.words: Freedom of movement needed by violinist
parts.note: a fiddler's bowing arm needs space beside it to work

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for adequate space to move is literally room for one's arm joint.

clue.text: One inclined to accept depth claimed by legendary swimmer

indicators.note: to accept means to take in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a leaner is one who leans, inclined

explanation.surface: A diver leaning forward takes the plunge, claimed by the legendary swimmer as his own.
explanation.walkthrough: Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to visit Hero in Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this youth swam the Hellespont each night to his lover Hero.

clue.text: Quick to recover and take exam again? That's about right

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: to resit is to sit an exam a second time
a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: A student fails, bounces back and retakes the exam, which seems about right.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough, buoyant person springs back quickly after setbacks.

clue.text: Quiet stroll turns into awkward walk

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
an amble is a leisurely stroll

explanation.surface: A peaceful saunter degenerates into clumsy shuffling.
explanation.definitionFit: To shuffle along clumsily is a shambling gait.

clue.text: Contract that's a link between banks

parts.note: a bridge links the two banks of a river

explanation.surface: A contract that connects two financial banks.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to shorten or condense it.

clue.text: Introduce as new title-holder

parts.note: sounds like presenting a new champion, but means raising someone to the peerage

explanation.definitionFit: To raise someone to the peerage gives them a noble title.

clue.text: Suspicions of light blows

definitions.meaning: hints or whispers, as in a breath of scandal

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both slight hints and gentle exhalations.

clue.text: Bishop is wearing headgear of religious type

annotationWithheld.why: Bishop is wearing headgear of religious type (7): B + IS inside HAT gives BHAIST, one A short of BAHAIST; no word supplies the second A
annotationWithheld.clue: Bishop is wearing headgear of religious type

clue.text: An aid to progress for those lacking drive?

definitions.text: An aid to progress for those lacking drive?

parts.words: An aid to progress for those lacking drive?
parts.note: sounds like help for the unmotivated, but describes a line for hauling a car whose engine has failed

explanation.definitionFit: A broken-down vehicle is pulled along by a line attached to another.

clue.text: Development of new hotel worth it for yield

indicators.note: development means reworking, so the letters of the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Building a new hotel is worth it for the return on investment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Development of' rearranges NEW HOTEL WORTH IT, all fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up or surrender is the idiom, from a boxer's corner conceding defeat.

clue.text: Wearing clothes very old and worn out

definitions.meaning: an archaic sense, attired or dressed

explanation.definitionFit: The word once meant attired, and now means exhausted.

clue.text: Singular import to gallery showing discrimination

indicators.note: import to means bring into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the Tate is the London art gallery
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: A unique acquisition by an art gallery shows refined judgment.
explanation.definitionFit: Discernment in matters of art and style is good aesthetic judgment.

clue.text: Communication system giving notice when entering port

indicators.note: entering means going into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port
an ad is an advertisement, a notice

explanation.surface: A signalling network posts a notice whenever a ship comes into harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Wireless broadcasting is a means of transmitting messages.

clue.text: Butterfly black and dull grey round the edge

parts.note: B is the pencil abbreviation for black
a rim is the circular edge of something
stone is a dull grey colour

explanation.surface: A butterfly is black and grey with a border round its wings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round the edge' is one unit, the rim, set between the black and the grey; the brimstone is a sulphur-yellow British butterfly.
explanation.definitionFit: A brimstone is a yellow butterfly common in Britain.

clue.text: Read silly letters in Times — extremely impractical

indicators.note: silly suggests the letters are jumbled foolishly into a new order

explanation.surface: A reader finds foolish letters in The Times wildly unrealistic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' rearranges the letters of READ and TIMES together; 'letters in' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of dreamy describes someone most lost in fantasy, the least practical.

clue.text: Sporting contest requiring constant temperature

parts.note: even means steady or constant

explanation.surface: A competition needs the weather to stay steady.
explanation.definitionFit: A single competition in a sports meeting is one item on the programme.
